provenance.exact_text: Resolve Korean maritime place names, ports, port entrances, islands, and curated reference points to canonical geometry and provenance.

bindings.attribute_definition: Classification of a wrecked or ruined ship.

global_listed_values.label: Non-Dangerous Wreck
global_listed_values.definition: A wreck which is not considered to be dangerous to surface navigation.

global_listed_values.label: Dangerous Wreck
global_listed_values.definition: A wreck submerged at such a depth as to be considered dangerous to surface navigation.

global_listed_values.label: Distributed Remains of Wreck
global_listed_values.definition: A substantively decayed wreck over which it is safe to navigate but which should be avoided for anchoring, taking the ground or ground fishing.

global_listed_values.label: Wreck Showing Mast/Masts
global_listed_values.definition: Wreck of which only the mast(s) is visible at the sounding datum indicated.

global_listed_values.label: Wreck Showing Any Portion of Hull or Superstructure
global_listed_values.definition: Wreck of which any portion of the hull or superstructure is visible at the sounding datum indicated.

bindings.attribute_definition: Indicates the relationship of the depth of a feature to the range of depth of the surrounding depth area.

global_listed_values.label: Within the Range of Depth of the Surrounding Depth Area
global_listed_values.definition: The depth corresponds to the depth range of the surrounding depth area; that is, the depth is not shoaler than the minimum depth of the surrounding depth area or deeper than the maximum depth of the surrounding depth area.

global_listed_values.label: Shoaler Than the Range of Depth of the Surrounding Depth Area
global_listed_values.definition: The depth is shoaler than the minimum depth of the surrounding depth area.

global_listed_values.label: Deeper Than the Range of Depth of the Surrounding Depth Area
global_listed_values.definition: The depth is deeper than the maximum depth of the surrounding depth area.

bindings.attribute_definition: Provides the name of an entity, defines the national language of the name, and provides the option to display the name at various system display settings.
The value of the vertical distance to the highest point of the feature, measured from a specified vertical datum.

A common unique identifier for entities which describe a single real-world feature, and which is used to identify instances of the feature in end-user systems where the feature may be included in multiple data product types.
The reliability of the value of a sounding.

global_listed_values.label: Depth Known
global_listed_values.definition: The depth from the chart datum to the seabed (or to the top of a drying feature) is known.

global_listed_values.label: Depth or Least Depth Unknown
global_listed_values.definition: The depth from chart datum to the seabed, or the shoalest depth of the feature is unknown.

global_listed_values.label: Doubtful Sounding
global_listed_values.definition: A depth that may be less than indicated.

global_listed_values.label: Unreliable Sounding
global_listed_values.definition: A depth that is considered to be an unreliable value.

global_listed_values.label: Least Depth Known
global_listed_values.definition: The shoalest depth over a feature is of known value.

global_listed_values.label: Least Depth Unknown, Safe Clearance at Value Shown
global_listed_values.definition: The least depth over a feature is unknown, but there is considered to be safe clearance at this depth.

global_listed_values.label: Value Reported (Not Surveyed)
global_listed_values.definition: Depth value obtained from a report, but not fully surveyed.

global_listed_values.label: Value Reported (Not Confirmed)
global_listed_values.definition: Depth value obtained from a report, which it has not been possible to confirm.

global_listed_values.label: Maintained Depth
global_listed_values.definition: The depth at which a channel is kept by human influence, usually by dredging.

global_listed_values.label: Not Regularly Maintained
global_listed_values.definition: Depths may be altered by human influence, but will not be routinely maintained.

global_listed_values.label: Not in Use
global_listed_values.definition: Use has ceased, but the facility still exists intact; disused.

global_listed_values.label: Periodic/Intermittent
global_listed_values.definition: Recurring at intervals.

global_listed_values.label: Reserved
global_listed_values.definition: Set apart for some specific use.

global_listed_values.definition: Meant to last only for a time.

global_listed_values.label: Private
global_listed_values.definition: Administered by an individual or corporation, rather than a State or a public body.

global_listed_values.label: Mandatory
global_listed_values.definition: Compulsory; enforced.

global_listed_values.label: Extinguished
global_listed_values.definition: No longer lit.

global_listed_values.label: Illuminated
global_listed_values.definition: Lit by flood lights, strip lights, etc.

global_listed_values.label: Historic
global_listed_values.definition: Famous in history; of historical interest.

global_listed_values.label: Public
global_listed_values.definition: Belonging to, available to, used or shared by, the community as a whole and not restricted to private use.

global_listed_values.label: Synchronized
global_listed_values.definition: Occur at a time, coincide in point of time, be contemporary or simultaneous.

global_listed_values.label: Watched
global_listed_values.definition: Looked at or observed over a period of time especially so as to be aware of any movement or change.

global_listed_values.label: Unwatched
global_listed_values.definition: Usually automatic in operation, without any permanently-stationed personnel to superintend it.

global_listed_values.label: Existence Doubtful
global_listed_values.definition: A feature that has been reported but has not been definitely determined to exist.

global_listed_values.label: Buoyed
global_listed_values.definition: Marked by buoys.

bindings.attribute_definition: Survey method used to obtain depth information.

global_listed_values.label: Found by Echo Sounder
global_listed_values.definition: The depth was measured by using an instrument that determines depth of water by measuring the time interval between emission of a sonic or ultrasonic signal and return of its echo from the bottom.

global_listed_values.label: Found by Side Scan Sonar
global_listed_values.definition: The depth was computed from a record produced by active sonar in which fixed acoustic beams are directed into the water perpendicularly to the direction of travel to scan the seabed and generate a record of the seabed configuration.

global_listed_values.label: Found by Multi Beam
global_listed_values.definition: The depth was measured by using a wide swath echo sounder that uses multiple beams to measure depths directly below and transverse to the ship's track.

global_listed_values.label: Found by Diver
global_listed_values.definition: The depth was determined by a person skilled in the practice of diving.

global_listed_values.label: Found by Lead Line
global_listed_values.definition: The depth was measured by using a line, graduated with attached marks and fastened to a sounding lead.

global_listed_values.label: Swept by Vertical Acoustic System
global_listed_values.definition: The given area has been swept using a system comprised of multiple echo sounder transducers attached to booms deployed from the survey vessel.

global_listed_values.label: Found by Electromagnetic Sensor
global_listed_values.definition: The depth was determined by using an instrument that compares electromagnetic signals.

global_listed_values.label: Photogrammetry
global_listed_values.definition: The science or art of obtaining reliable measurements from photographs.

global_listed_values.label: Satellite Imagery
global_listed_values.definition: The depth was determined by using instruments placed aboard an artificial satellite.

global_listed_values.label: Found by Levelling
global_listed_values.definition: The depth was determined by using levelling techniques to find the elevation of the point relative to a datum.

global_listed_values.label: Swept by Side Scan Sonar
global_listed_values.definition: The given area was determined to be free from navigational dangers to a certain depth by towing a side scan sonar.

global_listed_values.label: Found by LIDAR
global_listed_values.definition: The depth was measured by using an instrument that measures distance by emitting timed pulses of laser light and measuring the time between emission and reception of the reflected pulses.

global_listed_values.label: Synthetic Aperture Radar
global_listed_values.definition: A radar with a synthetic aperture antenna which is composed of a large number of elementary transducing elements. The signals are electronically combined into a resulting signal equivalent to that of a single antenna of a given aperture in a given direction.

global_listed_values.label: Hyperspectral Imagery
global_listed_values.definition: Term used to describe the imagery derived from subdividing the electromagnetic spectrum into very narrow bandwidths. These narrow bandwidths may be combined with or subtracted from each other in various ways to form images useful in precise terrain or target analysis.

global_listed_values.label: Mechanically Swept
global_listed_values.definition: The given area was determined to be free from navigational dangers to a certain depth by towing a line or object below the surface at the desired depth; or least depth(s) and position(s) within an area was identified using the same technique.

bindings.attribute_definition: The value of the measurement of a sounding relative to the chart datum.
The extent to which a feature, either natural or artificial, is visible from seaward.

global_listed_values.label: Visually Conspicuous
global_listed_values.definition: Term applied to an object either natural or artificial which is distinctly and notably visible from seaward.

global_listed_values.label: Not Visually Conspicuous
global_listed_values.definition: An object that may be visible from seaward, but cannot be used as a fixing mark and is not conspicuous.

global_listed_values.label: Prominent
global_listed_values.definition: Objects which are easily identifiable, but do not justify being classed as conspicuous.

bindings.attribute_definition: The effect of the surrounding water on an object.

global_listed_values.label: Partly Submerged at High Water
global_listed_values.definition: Partially covered and partially dry at high water.

global_listed_values.label: Always Dry
global_listed_values.definition: Not covered at high water under average meteorological conditions.

global_listed_values.label: Always Under Water/Submerged
global_listed_values.definition: Remains covered by water at all times under average meteorological conditions.

global_listed_values.label: Covers and Uncovers
global_listed_values.definition: Expression intended to indicate an area of a reef or other projection from the bottom of a body of water which periodically extends above and is submerged below the surface. Also referred to as dries or uncovers.

global_listed_values.label: Awash
global_listed_values.definition: Flush with, or washed by the waves at low water under average meteorological conditions.

global_listed_values.label: Subject to Inundation or Flooding
global_listed_values.definition: An area periodically covered by flood water, excluding tidal waters.

global_listed_values.label: Floating
global_listed_values.definition: Resting or moving on the surface of a liquid without sinking.

bindings.attribute_definition: The minimum scale at which the feature may be used for example for ECDIS presentation.
Textual information about the feature. The information may be provided as a string of text or as a file name of a single external text file that contains the text.
The file name of an externally referenced picture file.
The depth value determined for an underwater hazard of unknown depth, based on the depth of the surrounding area.
The depth value determined for seabed around an underwater hazard, based on the depth of the surrounding area.
